Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification — follow-up and action items

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call today — good to sync with you and the Acme Ops team. Summarizing the performance / SLO items we discussed and the next steps so we have a single place to track: 

High-level SLO targets (from your product team):
- p95 generation latency target: <100ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens)
- sustained throughput target: 2,000 concurrent streams (longer tail traffic expected)
- burst concurrency: up to 5,000 connections for short windows (30-120s)
- streaming: server-sent events for token streaming required (clients read partial tokens)
- max allowed p99 during business hours: 250ms

Network / Private deployment constraints we need to qualify:
- VPC peering / VPN path: type (VPC Peering, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect), regions/AZs involved, and whether cross-account peering is already in place
- Egress / firewall: list of outbound IPs we should allow, NAT/Proxy details, and egress bandwidth caps
- Internal latency budgets: expected intra-VPC hop latency (e.g., app -> inference nodes) and acceptable RTT to peered endpoints
- MTU, MTU blackhole risk, and any symmetric routing or policy-based routing in the path
- TLS interception / proxying (do you have any Layer 7 proxies that could delay streaming?)

Requested artifacts (if available):
1) Network diagram showing peering/VPC layout and egress path (attach as PNG/PDF)
2) Sample traceroute/latency measurements from your app lane to the target IPs (we can provide test IPs)
3) Expected concurrency distribution (normal vs. peak) and sample request size distribution (tokens per request)

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- We will provide a short test checklist and a set of public test endpoints (ips) by EOD tomorrow. (See attached redwood-performance-slo-checklist.pdf)
- Acme provides network diagram and current firewall/NAT egress IP list.
- Schedule a short test window with your network team (30-60 mins) to run traceroutes, iperf and a small streaming session to validate p95 targets.

Attachments: redwood-performance-slo-checklist.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If you can confirm who on your side we should loop in for the peering / firewall change (network ops contact + preferred maintenance window), I can coordinate with Jordan and Lauren on our infra side.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary — appreciate the checklist. Quick answers from the Acme Ops side and attached network diagram:

Environment & peering
- We are operating in AWS us-east-1 for the initial deployment.
- Peering method: cross-account VPC Peering between our app VPC (prod-app-vpc) and the partner/VPC where you will host the inference nodes (we can also consider Transit Gateway if needed).
- No Direct Connect in scope for this phase.

Egress / NAT / Firewall
- Egress traffic currently goes through a pair of NAT Gateways (public egress via managed NAT) with static Elastic IPs. We can whitelist outbound IPs on our side for the vendor endpoints.
- Firewall: Palo Alto cluster (managed) in front of the NAT layer - we can add rules for outbound TCP 443 to your endpoints.
- We have an outbound proxy for some teams but product lane does direct egress; proxy is not in the path for streaming sessions.

Performance numbers
- Expected baseline concurrency: ~1,800 active streams average; planned scaling to 2,500 in the first month. Peak bursts observed historically ~4,200 for 60-90s.
- Typical request size: 64-256 tokens.

Artifacts attached:
- acme-network-diagram.png
- sample-traceroute.txt (from a prod app host to 3rd-party endpoints)

We can run a test next Thursday 2028-04-19 between 09:00-11:00 EDT if that works for your infra team. Who should we expect on your side to coordinate?

Regards,
Sanjay Mehta

Thanks Sanjay - that all helps. A couple clarifications from our infra side and a short test plan: 

Clarifications
- For peering: VPC Peering is fine to start; Transit Gateway if you foresee multi-account scale or cross-region routing. We typically recommend same-region peering for lowest RTT.
- Egress IPs: we will provide a short allowlist (3 IPs) for our test endpoints. Can you confirm whether your Palo Alto cluster does any TCP proxying that would terminate TLS? You mentioned it sits in front of NAT - if it is doing TLS inspection that will break streaming.

Proposed quick test (30-45 mins) for 2028-04-19 10:00-10:45 EDT:
1) From a prod-app host run: traceroute + mtr to our test IPs (we'll share), record pings and 95th RTTs for 60s.
2) Run a short iperf3 test to measure bandwidth and latency (10s runs x 3).
3) Run a small streaming session with 50 concurrent clients from your app lane to validate p95 for short prompts (64 tokens). We'll stream token-by-token to verify no buffering.

What we need from you before the window:
- Confirm the list of source IPs for test traffic (we'll provide destination IPs).
- Point of contact on your side to kick off the test and apply temporary firewall changes if needed.

I'll be on the call along with Marissa and Lauren. If we observe buffering at the firewall/proxy we can iterate on bypass rules during the window.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Infra / Product Engineering | Redwood Inference
